newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian bank founder held on alleged fraud.
newsitem.headline: Romanian bank founder held on alleged fraud.

text.p: Romanian police on Wednesday said they had arrested on suspicion of fraud the former top shareholder in the debt-ridden Dacia Felix SA private bank.

Police spokesman Nicolae Chirion said by telephone that Sever Muresan was being held in connection with allegations of embezzlement, forgery and fraud. Chirion did not say how long the warrant was in effect, but prosecutors are empowered to issue renewable warrants of up to 30 days.
Dacia Felix, once a fast growing bank, awaits a court ruling on its reorganisation or liquidation after revealing bad debts of some $200 million and a 642.2 billion lei ($155.2 million) 1995 loss.

Last March, the central bank stripped Dacia Felix of most currency dealing rights. It banned 16 of its officials, including Muresan, from the banking industry, alleging "grave violations" of exchange and credit laws.
Muresan is a former Davis Cup tennis player who lives in France and counts former U.S. President George Bush among his friends. The bank said companies led by Muresan owe it some $200 million.
Muresan was held by police for a few hours in October, but prosecutors failed then to come up with a warrant. He has said in recent months that he has a plan to rescue the bank. ($1=4138 Lei)
